title: The quotient of a polynomial ring over a field by a separable polynomial is reduced
statement: Let $E$ be a field [def-weil-field], $E[T]$ the polynomial ring in one indeterminate [def-weil-polynomial-ring], and $Q\in E[T]$ a separable polynomial [def-pc-separable-polynomial] (there are $U,V\in E[T]$ with $UQ+VQ'=1$). Then the quotient ring $E[T]/(Q)$ by the principal ideal generated by $Q$ is reduced: if $g\in E[T]$ and $g^m\in(Q)$ for some integer $m\ge1$, then $g\in(Q)$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 030U (lemma-separable-extension-preserves-reducedness, label line 10152), first paragraph, line 10182: 'Since $P$ is separable this is a finite product of fields and we win' (here only the consequence 'reduced' is stated); tag 030U verified in literature/stacks-project/tags/tags (line 3961)

proof.text: The Bezout identity in [def-pc-separable-polynomial] implies that $Q$ is squarefree. Indeed, if $H^2$ divides $Q$, write $Q=H^2W$. The product rule for the formal polynomial derivative gives $Q'=2HH'W+H^2W'$, so $H$ divides both $Q$ and $Q'$. If $UQ+VQ'=1$, then $H$ divides $1$; hence $H$ is a unit. This proves precisely the square-divisor condition in [lem-weil-pbc-squarefree-polynomial-divides-power]. The argument also covers a nonzero constant $Q$, for which every divisor is a unit; $Q=0$ is excluded by the Bezout identity.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 030U (lemma-separable-extension-preserves-reducedness), lines 10175-10182; the source calls the quotient a finite product of fields and omits this squarefree calculation

proof.text: Let $g\in E[T]$ and $m\ge1$ with $g^m\in(Q)$. Membership in the principal ideal means exactly $Q\mid g^m$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-squarefree-polynomial-divides-power] with the squarefree condition from Step 1 to get $Q\mid g$, equivalently $g\in(Q)$. Thus every nilpotent class $g+(Q)$ in $E[T]/(Q)$ is zero: if its $m$-th power is zero, then $g^m\in(Q)$ and the preceding implication gives $g\in(Q)$. The quotient is reduced.
